prize_parts.citation: for the foundational analysis of bargaining with alternating offers

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged. B029 contains a remarkably parsimonious, mature, and enduring theoretical breakthrough: alternating-offers bargaining made strategic bargaining analytically tractable while yielding a clear solution prediction that has served as a canonical benchmark across theory and applications. The public configuration should deliberately isolate that achievement and credit Rubinstein alone. This is more proportionate than treating the ballot's associated bargaining-in-markets work as a symmetric three-person discovery. Relative to broader proposals, its narrower scope is compensated by unusually sharp conceptual unity and exact attribution.
statement.case_against: The proposed single-name citation recognizes only the alternating-offers core, not the full bargaining-in-markets programme described in B029. It is also a more abstract contribution than several alternatives with wider direct empirical or policy application. The committee must decide whether the exceptional clarity of the foundational result outweighs the broader field-level reach of other mature achievements.

responses.point: Friberg judges B029 foundational and mature but argues that Rubinstein is the indispensable principal contributor, so a three-name grouping would overstate symmetry of credit.
responses.response: I agree, and the round-2 comparison reinforces rather than changes my configuration. A prize can be tightly drawn around the alternating-offers breakthrough without purporting to reward every related contribution to bargaining in markets. That boundary makes the single-name attribution a strength rather than an omission.

responses.point: Dreber Almenberg favors B041 because its formal and experimental work on reciprocity, fairness, and inequity aversion durably changed analysis of incentives, cooperation, and labour relations, while acknowledging heterogeneous phenomena and contextual variation.
responses.response: I continue to regard B041 as a leading alternative and agree that its influence does not require every preference estimate to be invariant across contexts. Nonetheless, its broad theoretical and empirical programme leaves more residual questions about the unity and outer boundary of the achievement than B029. Rubinstein's result provides a more precisely identifiable discovery and a correspondingly cleaner attribution.

responses.point: Boppart describes B018 as a mature and broadly applied dynamic-panel methodology with clear attribution, while noting finite-sample and instrument-proliferation limitations.
responses.response: That is a serious competing case and explains why B018 remains my principal methodological alternative. Its limitations do not erase its importance. I retain B029 because it supplied a foundational strategic framework rather than an empirical-methods toolkit, and because its citation can identify one central intellectual contribution without overclaiming adjacent work.

uncertainties: Whether the committee considers the restricted alternating-offers citation sufficiently representative of the broader B029 ballot.
How to weigh B029's exceptionally exact attribution against the broader practical influence of B018 and B041.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile; no new candidate-specific conflict is disclosed.
